title: Impact of a Diagnosis or Lack of a Diagnosis of Endometriosis Via a Saliva Test on Pain Catastrophizing, Quality of Life, Symptoms of Anxiety and Depression, and Treatment Adherence
official: Impact of a Diagnosis or Lack of a Diagnosis of Endometriosis Via a Saliva Test on Pain Catastrophizing, Quality of Life, Symptoms of Anxiety and Depression, and Treatment Adherence
summary:
This non-interventional study aims to assess the impact of an endometriosis diagnosis obtained through a salivary test (Ziwig Endotest®) on pain-related cognitions, quality of life, mood, and treatment adherence, comparingthese outcomes with those of individuals who underwent the same salivary test but received a negative result and were therefore not diagnosed with endometriosis.

Participation in this study will contribute to advancing research in the field of endometriosis diagnosis and multidisciplinary management by expanding current knowledge of diagnostic protocols and their impact on pain, quality of life, treatment adherence, and potential psychiatric comorbidities. The investigators hope to enhance understanding of endometriosis and pelvic pain symptomatology in order to develop new therapeutic strategies, including psychological interventions or integrated psychological care, that better address the needs and specific characteristics of patients whether or not they receive a diagnosis of endometriosis.
criteria:
Inclusion Criteria:

* Patients eligible for an endotest as part of the innovation package at Jeanne de Flandre Hospital
* Patients between 18 to 43 years old
* Understand and can communicate in French
* Having received medical images that do not allow the diagnosis of endometriosis
* Presenting with symptoms suggestive of endometriosis
* Giving oral non-opposition to participe in the study
* Beneficiary of health insurance coverage
* Having normal visual and auditory acuity or corrected to normal levels

Exclusion Criteria:

* Minors, adults under guardianship, under judicial protection, and persons deprived of liberty
* Refusal to participate after receiving clear and fair information about the study
* Sensory, visual or auditory inability to participate in the study
* Personal history of neurological disorders or current neurological disorder
* Consumtion of toxic substances other than tobacco and alcohol.
* Personal history of psychiatric disorders or current psychiatric disorders other than anxiety, depressive, or trauma- and stress-related disorders
* Use of psychotropic medications
* Pregnant or breastfeeding women
